screening_decisions.reason: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial applying nitroprusside gel prior to IUD insertion; self-reported insertion pain measured. Meets RCT and pain-prevention criteria.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of ibuprofen 800 mg taken prior to IUD insertion; self-reported pain at/after insertion measured. Meets criteria.

Randomized trial of bladder filling (delayed vs immediate emptying). Although pain was measured, the intervention targets procedural ease rather than prevention of insertion-related pain per protocol. Exclude per strict criteria.
Randomized clinical trial comparing intracervical lidocaine injection vs NSAID before LNG-IUS insertion; self-reported pain immediately, 2h, and 6h post-insertion assessed. Meets criteria.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT of ibuprofen prophylaxis prior to LNG-IUS insertion; self-reported pain at tenaculum and insertion recorded. Meets criteria.
Double-blind, multicenter RCT of vaginal misoprostol vs placebo administered prior to IUD insertion; insertion pain and complications assessed. Meets criteria.
RCT in nulliparous women: buccal misoprostol vs placebo prior to insertion; self-reported pain at multiple procedural time points (including tenaculum and insertion). Meets criteria.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of sublingual misoprostol prior to consecutive LNG-IUS replacement; pain at insertion reported. Although primary aim was ease of insertion, pain outcomes present. Include conservatively.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 400 mg ibuprofen prophylaxis before IUD insertion; self-reported insertion pain measured. Meets criteria.
Single-blind randomized controlled trial of sublingual misoprostol (with diclofenac) vs diclofenac alone 1h prior to IUD insertion; pain and complications outcomes. Meets criteria.
Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled study of ibuprofen dosing around IUD insertion; pain during insertion and up to days after assessed. Meets criteria.
Randomized, double-blind clinical trial comparing tramadol, naproxen, and placebo 1h prior to IUD insertion; VAS pain during insertion measured. Meets criteria.

Double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial of misoprostol vs placebo before insertion in nulliparous women; provider ease and patient-reported pain (immediately prior and after insertion) assessed. Meets criteria.
Randomized, double-blind clinical trial of intracervical 2% lidocaine gel vs placebo prior to sounding and insertion; self-reported pain at procedural time points measured. Meets criteria.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study of vaginal nitroglycerin gel prior to IUD placement; patient-reported procedural pain measured. Meets criteria.
Randomized trial comparing 1% lidocaine paracervical block vs no anesthetic prior to IUD insertion; self-reported pain at tenaculum and insertion measured. Meets criteria.
Randomized controlled trial (3-arm) of intracervical lidocaine gel vs lubricant vs no intervention; self-reported pain during insertion measured. Meets criteria.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study of intrauterine infusion of 2% lidocaine vs saline 3 min prior; self-reported pain at tenaculum and insertion measured. Meets criteria.
Randomized controlled trial of sublingual misoprostol plus diclofenac vs diclofenac alone 1h prior to insertion in nulliparous women; pain and ease of insertion assessed. Meets criteria.
Randomized, double-blind clinical trial of vaginal misoprostol 4h prior to insertion in nulligravidas; moderate-to-severe insertion pain reduced; outcomes include self-reported pain. Meets criteria.
Randomized trial of lavender aromatherapy vs placebo inhalation before insertion; self-reported pain post-insertion assessed. Intervention intended to reduce anxiety/pain. Include conservatively.
Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of self-administered misoprostol vs placebo 3–4h prior; self-reported pain immediately post-insertion and at discharge measured. Meets criteria.

Randomized, placebo-controlled phase-II trial of a novel topical lidocaine formulation applied to portio/cervix/uterus prior to IUD insertion; self-reported pain within 10 min and at 30 min measured. Meets criteria.
Prospective, single-blinded controlled study of paracervical block vs placebo vs no treatment; randomization not described/unclear. Protocol includes only RCTs. Exclude.
Randomized trial in nulliparous women of misoprostol vs placebo prior to insertion; primary outcome was pain at insertion; provider ease also assessed. Meets criteria.

Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of self-administered 2% lidocaine vaginal gel vs placebo 5 min prior; self-reported pain at multiple procedural time points measured. Meets criteria.
Narrative/practice description of intracervical anesthesia technique; not a randomized controlled trial.
Prospective cohort study comparing pain by prior vaginal delivery; not an interventional RCT.
Qualitative study of non-users’ perceptions; not an interventional RCT on insertion-related pain prevention.
Narrative/practical review; not an interventional RCT.
GRADE methodology paper; not relevant to interventional RCTs on IUC insertion pain prevention.
Committee Opinion/guideline; not an interventional RCT on insertion pain prevention.
Review article on pain management; not an interventional RCT.
Review on misoprostol in gynecology; not an interventional RCT specific to IUC insertion pain prevention.
Observational study of expected vs actual pain with a specific insertion technique; not randomized.
GRADE methodology paper; not an interventional RCT.
Predictive study using ultrasound/history to predict difficult/painful insertion; not an interventional RCT.
Review on evidence-based pain management; not an interventional RCT.
Systematic review of intrauterine anesthesia across gynecologic procedures; not a primary RCT specific to our inclusion.
Observational study on pre-fitting analgesia use/anxiety; not a randomized trial.
Technical report/guideline on contraception for adolescents; not an interventional RCT.
Meta-analysis of analgesic options; not a primary RCT.
RCT of nitric oxide donors for cervical ripening prior to surgical termination (first trimester), not IUD insertion.
Survey of practitioner techniques/policies; not an interventional RCT.
Methodology for prospective meta-analysis; not a primary interventional RCT.
Commentary arguing against misoprostol before insertion; not a primary RCT.
Randomized double-blind trial of meptazinol to treat pain following IUD insertion; this treats post-insertion pain rather than preventing insertion-related pain per protocol. Exclude.

Randomized clinical trial (lavender vs sesame oil vs control) with aromatherapy prior to insertion; self-reported pain after insertion measured; intervention intended for pain relief. Include conservatively.
Technique description for paracervical block; not a randomized controlled trial.
Cochrane review of NSAIDs for bleeding/pain associated with IUD use; not a primary RCT focused on insertion pain prevention.
